text:
elaine (support): FYI we have a high-priority escalation from AcmeHealth — after last night's canary rollout customers are reporting that structured JSON output is missing some keys (order_id, items array) in about ~5-10% of responses. they rely on strict schema.

connor (eng): ack. which model/version and rollout percentage? any errors in the API logs?

elaine (support): model param: "open-llm-v2-structured" (rolled as v2.1 -> v2 default); deploy-bot shows canary 20% at 2024-10-24T02:14:03Z then auto-increased to 100% at 2024-10-24T03:40:11Z. customer reported regressions starting ~03:50Z. No 500 errors; responses are 200 with JSON body but keys missing or truncated strings.

deploy-bot: Rollout event: model=open-llm-v2-structured, from=stable-v2.0, rollout=0%->20%->100%, initiated_by=marco (ml), runbook=rollout/v2.1.md :rocket:

marco (ml): I triggered the rollout. We did change prompt framing and added extra post-processing step to coerce JSON using a lightweight schema sanitizer. Maybe that interaction is the culprit.

lucy (support): customer provided example responses (they expect items array, price and order_id). Their original request and two responses below.

elaine (support): REQUEST:
```
POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate
{
  "model": "open-llm-v2-structured",
  "input": "create order for user 123 with items: [\"widget\", \"gizmo\"] return strict json schema",
  "stream": false
}
```

EXPECTED (schema):
```
{
  "order_id": "string",
  "user_id": 123,
  "items": [{"sku":"string","qty":int}],
  "total": float
}
```

RESPONSES CUSTOMER SAW (examples):
1) MISSING order_id and items truncated:
```
{ "user_id": 123, "total": 19.99 }
```
2) MALFORMED item object (string instead of object):
```
{ "order_id": "A-001", "user_id": 123, "items": ["widget", "gizmo"], "total": 19.99 }
```

elaine (support): customer says this started *after* our rollout; they had no issues on stable v2.0. They also ran validation against their JSON schema and it failed for ~8% of calls.

connor (eng): can you paste the request ids / logs for those failed responses? need headers (model, content-type, x-request-id, latency) plus the full response body. Also which SDK / language are they using — streaming vs non-streaming changes output handling.

elaine (support): provided two request ids: req_8a1f, req_8a23. latency for those was 450ms and 180ms respectively. Both 200 OK. Attached logs: 
```
[req_8a1f] model=open-llm-v2-structured, latency=450ms, tokens_in=24, tokens_out=32
response: {"user_id":123,"total":19.99}
[req_8a23] model=open-llm-v2-structured, latency=180ms, tokens_in=24, tokens_out=45
response: {"order_id":"A-001","user_id":123,"items":["widget","gizmo"],"total":19.99}
```

marco (ml): hmm tokens_out small for first one. Could be early stop / max_tokens set too low or our post-processor accidentally truncating when it detects non-JSON tokens. We did add a regex-based sanitizer that drops keys with non-matching shapes. Might be over-eager.

connor (eng): also check if streaming flag misinterpreted by SDK: some SDKs stitch chunks and then run JSON parse; if we changed newline / chunk delimiters it could leave out trailing brackets in some cases. But requests were non-streaming per the request sample.

sre-bot: Alert: spike in validation failures for schema=open_orders_v1 in region=us-east-1 starting 2024-10-24T03:48Z. Failure rate from baseline 0.2% -> 6.7%.

lucy (support): customer provided repro script using curl — they ran it 1000x and saw ~7% failures. sharing snippet: 
```
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -d '{"model":"open-llm-v2-structured","input":"create order for user 123 with items: [\"widget\", \"gizmo\"] return strict json schema","stream":false}' \
  | jq . || echo "PARSE FAIL"
done
```

connor (eng): good repro. action items: (1) collect full response bodies + X-Request-IDs + timestamps for failed samples, (2) roll back traffic to v2.0 for affected customers as an emergency mitigation, (3) add a short-term patch to post-processing to avoid dropping keys — make it permissive not strict. I'll take 1 and 2.

marco (ml): I'll pause further rollouts and revert the regex sanitizer. I'm pushing a rollback to stable config now.

deploy-bot: Deployment action: rollback model=open-llm-v2-structured -> stable-v2.0, initiated_by=connor (eng), started=2024-10-24T04:05:12Z, result=partial (affected customers still on cached routing until TTL expires).

elaine (support): customer asked if this could be related to quantization or kernel selection (they saw weird truncated items). Any chance?

marco (ml): unlikely at runtime — model weights same, only prompt + sanitizer changed. But quantization sometimes changes logits around boundary tokens; however both responses are syntactically valid JSON just missing keys — smells like post-processing.

connor (eng): found two failing logs where our sanitizer matched a naive pattern: it was dropping keys if the value didn't match the strict type check (e.g., expecting object for items but saw array of strings -> dropped entire key). that's a bug. patching to coerce arrays into object items if possible.

lucy (support): customer is asking for a concrete timeline to full fix and for temporary workaround (they can't rollback to old client quickly).

connor (eng): timeline: hotfix to sanitizer in 30-45m (less strict checks, log mismatch instead of drop), then we monitor schema failure rate. For customers that need immediate relief we can route them to stable-v2.0 via per-tenant routing (support can request tenant reroute).

elaine (support): passing to customer: we'll (1) apply hotfix within an hour, (2) offer tenant routing to stable v2.0 as temporary mitigation, (3) follow up with postmortem and test-suite improvements.

marco (ml): follow-ups: add unit tests for sanitizer behavior, add synthetic evals that validate schema adherence across canary traffic, and add metric for dropped-keys count.

sre-bot: Action created: SRV-1342 "Schema sanitizer overzealous key dropping" assigned to connor (eng) priority=P1.

lucy (support): customer responded: appreciate fast response, asked for a one-line mitigation they can use immediately if we can't route — they can append a wrapper to their client to re-run schema coercion locally (we provided snippet).

elaine (support): local coercion snippet we provided: 
```
# naive JS fallback
try {
  const parsed = JSON.parse(respBody);
  if (!parsed.order_id) parsed.order_id = "UNKNOWN";
  if (!Array.isArray(parsed.items)) parsed.items = parsed.items ? parsed.items.map(x=>({sku:x,qty:1})) : [];
} catch(e) { /* escalate */ }
```

connor (eng): I'll keep monitoring. once sanitizer reverted and hotfixed we'll run the customer's 1000x test internally. please tag me on any failing request ids.

elaine (support): thanks all. >closing loop with customer after hotfix and a short postmortem. :thumbsup:

marco (ml): noting for postmortem: we should not couple lightweight output sanitizers with aggressive drop semantics. also, we should have test harness that runs schema validators against canary output before full rollout.

sre-bot: SRV-1342 moved -> In Progress.

connor (eng): hotfix deployed 2024-10-24T04:28Z, sanitizer now logs mismatches instead of dropping keys. initial monitoring: schema failure rate down to 0.6% at 04:40Z. will run internal 1000x now.

elaine (support): customer ran quick test and reports failures down to ~0.5%. they are happy for now and requested a formal postmortem and improved canary tests.

lucy (support): creating follow-up ticket CUST-9921 for customer communication and SOC-approved timeline for full postmortem.

elaine (support): thread closing notes: root cause = overzealous schema sanitizer in post-processing introduced during v2.1 rollout; mitigations = rollback/tenant routing + hotfix changing drop->log + client-side coercion snippet; next steps = postmortem, add unit tests/synthetic schema checks in canary pipeline.
